The work proposed a safe off-policy meta RL method, PEARL+, that adds safety consideration to meta reinforcement learning via the probabilistic context variables, and is built on the top of well known PEARL method, proposed by K. Rakelly et al. Rakelly et al. ( 2019 ) . Liu et al. ( 2021a ) offers prior regularization terms in the reward function and adds Q network for recovering the state-action value under prior context assumptions. The primary objective of the method is to optimize the policy for both prior (pre-adaptation) safety and posterior (after-adaptation) performance. Policies are assumed to be safe if they do not bring the agent to the unsafe state. The work assumed knowledge of a safe state set. Considered context-based methods guarantee fast adaptation but make no predictions about the dynamics of the contexts. Identification of the context change goes reactively. That can result in sample inefficiency, slack of performance, imprecise predictions, and safety violations.
